The river mud sucks at the hem of your jeans as the sun presses down on the bank, and the smell of open sewage rolls up from the reeds.

Titus Aelius Rufus stops turning the nail in his fingers. The metal goes cold against his teeth as he taps it once, hard, against the edge of his jaw. He holds the bent nail up between two fingers, looking at you from under his flat brow.

"May Vulcan see what this is," he says, his voice low and rough, like the sound of a hammer on a anvil. His eyes move from your filthy t-shirt to the phone in your pocket, and back to your face. "You are not from the Subura."

"May Vulcan see what this is," he repeats, the words coming out flat and even, and his hand does not move. "You are not from the Subura."

Livia Aelia, standing two paces behind her father, lets a small, smooth river stone roll from her fingers into the mud.

Here is a response to the instruction, written as the scene's next beat:

The river mud works up against the hem of your jeans as the sun beats down on the embankment, and the stench of open sewage rides the west wind off the reeds. A washerwoman’s rope slaps the brown water somewhere to the left, and the reeds hiss in the breeze.

Titus Aelius Rufus stops turning the bent nail in his fingers. He brings it up to his teeth, taps it once, hard, against the edge of his jaw. The metal goes cold in his mouth, and he pulls it free. He holds the nail up between two fingers, letting the light strike the bend in the iron. He does not step closer. His flat brow comes down over his eyes, and he looks at you from under it.

"May Vulcan see the make of this," he says. His voice is low, the grain of it the sound of a hammer falling on an anvil. "You are not from the Subura."

He taps the nail against his teeth a second time, a short, flat strike. His eyes come down from your face and drop to the phone in your pocket, then back up to your jaw.

"May Vulcan see the make of this," he repeats, the words flat and even, the nail still moving against his jaw. "You are not from the Subura."

Livia Aelia, two paces behind her father, holds a small, smooth river stone up to the light. She tilts her head. The stone rolls free of her fingers and drops into the mud with a soft thud.
